prompt: `mypy` (strict mode, configured in `pyproject.toml`) reports errors in `src/`. Fix them so that `mypy` passes, without `# type: ignore`, `cast`, `Any`, or changes to the mypy configuration.
bash_commands: cat pyproject.toml; find src -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l; mypy 2>&1 | tail -40
cat src/trailhead/elevation.py src/trailhead/pace.py src/trailhead/report.py src/trailhead/track.py; ls tests
cat README* | head -80; grep -rn -i "none\|missing\|lost\|,$" tests | head -40; git log --oneline | head

mypy && ruff check && python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3
cat > $TMPDIR/t.py <<'EOF'
from trailhead.track import parse_track
from trailhead.report import summarise
t = parse_track("lat,lon,ele\n0,0,\n0,0.01,100\n0,0.02,\n0,0.03,130\n")
print(t.elevations(), summarise(t))
EOF
PYTHONPATH=src python $TMPDIR/t.py
printf 'lat,lon,ele\n0,0,\n0,0.01,\n' > $TMPDIR/none.csv; PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead summary $TMPDIR/none.csv; echo "exit $?"
mypy && ruff check && python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3

PYTHONPATH=src python -c '
from trailhead.track import parse_track
from trailhead.report import summarise
t = parse_track("lat,lon,ele
0,0,
0,0.01,100
0,0.02,
0,0.03,130
")
print(t.elevations(), summarise(t))
'
printf 'lat,lon,ele
0,0,
0,0.01,
' > "$TMPDIR/none.csv"; PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead summary "$TMPDIR/none.csv"; echo "exit $?"
